title: Before Growing the Business, Build the Capacity to Serve It
summary: Build insurance service capacity before chasing a bigger book. Check the service work growth will add before the queue does.
body_markdown:
# **Before Growing the Business, Build the Capacity to Serve It**


A bigger book looks like progress until the extra service work lands on people who are still finishing last week's work. The announcement moves faster than the operation.


During[our podcast with Sandip Bhadury](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eDKTaVR8Gmc&t=1278s) , he talked about the order he would use while an insurer is still being built. He had just been describing that early build. Then he put the ability to handle the work ahead of the chase for business.


He called this his own view, and said others may differ. He would not push hard for business at the start of that phase. He expects business to come once delivery starts. The ability to handle the work should be in place before the business itself.


Later in the same episode,[around 23:45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eDKTaVR8Gmc&t=1425s) , he added a second step. When the market can see that the operation handles the work and delivers what was promised, trust follows. He expects the business to follow that trust. Treat the expectation as his judgment, and test it against the work the team already carries.


*The growth announcement is the visible part. The service queue is the part the team inherits.*


## **Count the work a bigger book adds**


Insurance service capacity is a list of work, written before anyone sets a growth target. Before a growth push, write down what the new volume will create for your team.


- **Questions:** Cover questions, claim updates and payment checks. Each new customer adds more of them.
- **Exceptions:** The case that doesn't match the usual answer, and needs a person who can see what has already been said.
- **Delivery proof:** What the customer receives, and how long that takes once the team is already busy.


Our article on[distribution that scales](https://www.curacel.co/post/scalable-insurance-distribution-without-operational-debt) describes the backlog that shows up after a partner launch. The check here comes earlier. Can the current operation serve the next book before anyone goes looking for it?


## **See whether the team can finish that work**


Capacity is the volume a team can close without dropping the standard it has already promised. A growth plan that only works with overtime has already run out of room.


- **Known volume:** Count what the team closes in a normal week, including the repeat questions.
- **Spare room:** Add the volume the growth plan assumes. If the only way through is longer hours, the operation is behind the plan.
- **Owner:** Name who on your team watches the queue, and who can pause a campaign when service starts to slip.


Sandip was arguing for serving the work already in hand before collecting more of it. A team that is already late doesn't become reliable because the book gets larger.


*New volume on one side. The work the team can finish, to the promised standard, on the other.*

## **Keep judgment with the people who own the answer**


Some of the new volume is the same question, asked again. A support agent can take that repeat work from knowledge the team has added, and from records it has connected. The team keeps the cases that need a decision.


- **Added knowledge:** Website pages and files the team has checked, so the answer comes from that material.
- **Connected records:** Customer, claim and payment data, where those systems are connected. They remain the source of record.
- **Handoff:** A person gets the question, the history and the details already collected when judgment is needed.


In agent assist, the suggested reply shows its source, so a person can review it before sending. On a live channel, the team still chooses when the agent may answer.


That can add capacity for repeat service. It doesn't replace capital, underwriting or staffing. It is not the rest of the operating platform. A faster reply on a familiar question doesn't show that your whole operation can carry a bigger book.


## **The Takeaway**


Before growing the business, build the capacity to serve it. Sandip offered that as his own view. Handle the work first, and let delivery earn trust. If your team can't finish the service work the current book creates, a bigger book adds to the queue.
